correctness.rationale: For all finite q and parts a,b,c>=2, first count the a×b block by exact rank r, split off its 2r nondegenerate alternating block, rank the remaining rectangular block U by s, and split off another 2s block. The residual rank is precisely the symplectic pullback form T_0^t J^-1 T_0 on the c-s-dimensional kernel of U; T has q^(2rs) free choices on a complementary s-space. The H sum counts each pullback via the unique radical R of the image W, isotropic h-planes, nondegenerate 2j-planes of R-perp/R, and onto maps. These steps cover all matrices exactly once, yielding the full rank spectrum. Odd-characteristic class-two central-character decomposition gives q^(n-2t) irreducible characters of degree q^t per rank-2t edge label. The finite verifier independently exhausts twelve cases over q=2,3,4, eight directly enumerated pullbacks, and 125 pullback normalizations; these checks corroborate but do not prove the general theorem.

originality.rationale: The published Rossmann (2022) question concerns exactly the degree multiplicities of graphical groups and their alternating rank matrices, but does not furnish a complete-tripartite rank enumeration. The Rossmann–Voll (2025) join theorem determines ask zeta functions encoding average kernel sizes, not explicitly each fixed-field rank fiber. A coning rank recurrence was inspected in full and does cover K_{1,a,b} but not any K_{a,b,c} with all a,b,c>=2. Published tree and cycle strata are on different graphs. Direct semantically targeted searches found no equivalent full K_{a,b,c} formula. This is evidence for, not a logical proof of, priority; a historical symplectic equivalent remains a residual risk.

value.rationale: The exact rank-resolved spectrum solves the natural graphical-group character-degree enumeration question for all complete tripartite graphs with three non-singleton parts, an infinite graph family not reached by existing universal-vertex closure. It gives complete degree multiplicities rather than group order, average kernel size, or isolated values. The structural symplectic pullback lemma is independently useful in constrained alternating-matrix counting; the smallest nontrivial example K_(2,2,2) exhibits multiple rank strata. Significance is grounded in a published explicit problem and natural parameter family, not a merely large computation.
